# CXF / age interoperability fixture

All contents and credentials are synthetic. `external.json` follows CXF 1.0.
`external.age` was encrypted independently with the Go age CLI 1.3.1:

```console
age --passphrase -o external.age external.json
```

The public test passphrase is `synthetic interop fixture passphrase`.
The fixture verifies decoding the open encryption format without using our
own encryptor to construct the test input. Do not replace it with a file
generated by the Rust code under test.

`hybrid-key.txt`, `hybrid-recipient.txt`, and `hybrid.age` were generated with
the same independent Go age 1.3.1 CLI:

```console
age-keygen -pq -o hybrid-key.txt
age-keygen -y hybrid-key.txt > hybrid-recipient.txt
age -R hybrid-recipient.txt -o hybrid.age external.json
```

The committed identity is **public test material**, never a production key.
Tests copy it into a private temporary file because git does not preserve mode
0600. The opt-in `hybrid_go_cli_interoperability` Rust test also checks the
reverse direction with a fresh FactorSeal export and the external Go CLI.
